extraction_metadata.scope_note: This is an institutional practice policy, not a primary empirical study. Policy definitions and recommendations are represented with other or author_conclusion atoms. The medication treatment table is atomized one row at a time. The bibliography is not atomized.

atoms.canonical_statement: The DUHS policy aims to outline care for pediatric and adult patients at risk for or experiencing extravasation of intravenous or intraarterial medications or infusions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Purpose: To outline the care of the pediatric or adult patient at risk for or with an extravasation of intravenous or intraarterial medications and/or infusion.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy applies to Duke University Hospital at both campuses and Duke Regional Hospital.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Applicability: Duke University Hospital (DUH) (both campuses) ... Duke Regional Hospital (DRH)

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplied document is DUHS policy/procedure document 7259, revision 2, with effective date August 23, 2024 and status Published.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Document ID: 7259 Revision Number: 2 Status: Published ... Effective Date: 08/23/2024

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy states that prompt treatment is imperative because extravasation injury can begin at the time of the event and may lead to major soft tissue injury.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The damage to the tissues can begin at the time of extravasation; therefore, prompt treatment is imperative to decrease the extent of the injury.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy advises use of a CVAD or PICC for certain irritant and vesicant medications whenever possible and appropriate, with pharmacy consultation about peripheral venous access suitability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To reduce the incidence of extravasations, certainirritant and vesicant medications should be administered in a CVAD or PICC whenever possible and appropriate. Check with pharmacy to determine if medications are appropriate for peripheral venous access.

atoms.canonical_statement: RNs and LPNs may treat extravasation infusions after demonstrating competency.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Personnel: RNs and LPNs may treat extravasation infusions after demonstrating competency.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy defines infiltration as unintentional leakage of a nonvesicant solution into surrounding tissue.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Infiltration - Unintentional leakage of a nonvesicant solution into surrounding tissue.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy defines extravasation as leakage of a vesicant solution from the vein into surrounding tissue.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Extravasation - Leakage of a vesicant solution from the vein into the surrounding tissue

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy defines a vesicant as a solution that can injure surrounding tissue and may cause blistering, tissue sloughing, or necrosis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Vesicant - Solution that can cause injury or damage to surrounding tissue. Vesicants can cause blistering, tissue sloughing, or necrosis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy describes hyaluronidase as a subcutaneous treatment used around the injection site to reduce tissue damage when given within 2 hours for specified medication extravasations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Hyaluronidase injection - Administered subcutaneously around the injection site to reduce tissue damage when treatment occurs within 2 hours of extravasation of specific medications.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy states that hyaluronidase increases the absorption rate of fluid threefold to fivefold when used for IV medication extravasation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: When hyaluronidase is used to treat IV medication extravasations, the increased rate of absorption of fluid is 3-5 fold.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy describes phentolamine as a subcutaneous local vasodilator used around the injection site to reduce tissue injury after selected medication extravasations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Phentolamine injection - Administered subcutaneously around the injection site to reduce tissue damage ... Phentolamine causes local vasodilation

atoms.canonical_statement: Stop the infusion immediately after an extravasation is recognized.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A. Stop the infusion.

atoms.canonical_statement: Attempt to aspirate fluid from the IV catheter at the hub after stopping the infusion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: B. Attempt to aspirate fluid from the IV catheter at the hub.

atoms.canonical_statement: Assess the size of the affected area and outline it with a marker.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 1. Size of affected area. Outline the area with a marker.

atoms.canonical_statement: Record the name, volume, and concentration of the extravasated medication or medications.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 2. Name, volume and concentration of extravasated drug(s).

atoms.canonical_statement: Assess site color, edema, pain, skin breakdown, and drainage every 2 hours after the event until signs and symptoms resolve.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Color (redness or blanching), edema, pain, skin breakdown, and drainage at the extravasation site every 2 hours after the event until signs and symptoms resolved.

atoms.canonical_statement: Perform a neurovascular assessment of the affected limb and notify the provider of any change in neurovascular status.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Complete a neurovascular assessment of affected limb including pulse presence, capillary refill time, color, temperature, sensation and joint movement. Notify the provider of any alterations to neurovascular status.

atoms.canonical_statement: Elevate the affected site if possible.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: D. Elevate site if possible.

atoms.canonical_statement: Do not apply pressure to the extravasation site.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: E. Do not apply pressure to the extravasation site.

atoms.canonical_statement: Notify the provider to determine whether antidote or other treatment is needed; pharmacist and provider consultation can guide treatment selection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: F. Notify Provider to determine need for antidote/treatment. Consultation with a pharmacist and provider can help determine appropriate antidote or treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: If the extravasated medication is not listed in the treatment table, contact a pharmacist about whether an antidote or treatment is needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: If the medication that was infusing is not listed in the chart below, and extravasation is suspected, contact your pharmacist about the need for an antidote/treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: Remove the IV only when it is no longer needed for antidote administration; the ICN/SCN instruction is to remove the catheter immediately.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only remove the IV if no longer necessary for Antidote (see below) a. ICN/SCN: Remove Catheter immediately

atoms.canonical_statement: For hyaluronidase treatment, remove IV access from the extravasation site.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Remove IV access from site of extravasation

atoms.canonical_statement: Hyaluronidase used for this procedure is not for IV administration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Not for IV administration.

atoms.canonical_statement: Use hyaluronidase 150 units/mL for administration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Use hyaluronidase 150 units/ml for administration

atoms.canonical_statement: Prepare five hyaluronidase injections of 0.2 mL each; the ICN/SCN instruction specifies 0.1 mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Prepare 5 injections of 0.2 mL each. ICN/SCN: 0.1 mL

atoms.canonical_statement: Administer five subcutaneous hyaluronidase injections of 0.2 mL around the circumference of the affected area, using a new 25-gauge needle for each injection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Infiltrate area with by making 5 subcutaneous injections of 0.2 mL each, around the circumference of affected area with a new 25-gauge needle for each injection.

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy states that hyaluronidase is most effective when administered within 1 to 2 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most effective if administered within 1-2 hours

atoms.canonical_statement: Apply a dry gauze dressing after hyaluronidase administration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Apply dry gauze dressing to affected area.

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, the phentolamine dose should not exceed 0.1 mg/kg or 2.5 mg total.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dose should not exceed 0.1mg/kg or 2.5 mg total

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, dilute phentolamine 5 mg in 10 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to yield 0.5 mg/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dilute 5 mg in 10 ml 0.9% Sodium Chloride injection (Yielding a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL)

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, withdraw remaining medication from the IV catheter before phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Withdraw any remaining medication from the IV catheter

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, administer phentolamine subcutaneously around the site in small divided doses of 0.1 to 0.2 mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In small divided doses (0.1 - 0.2 ml) administer dose subcutaneously around the site.

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, inject phentolamine into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Solution should be injected into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

atoms.canonical_statement: For ICN/SCN patients, visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth are listed as signs of effective phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth at the site of extravasation are signs of effective treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, the phentolamine dose should not exceed 0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg or 5 mg total.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dose should not exceed 0.1 to 0.2mg/kg or 5 mg total

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, dilute phentolamine 5 mg in 10 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to yield 0.5 mg/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dilute 5 mg in 10 ml 0.9% Sodium Chloride injection (Yielding a concentration of 0.5 mg/ml)

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, withdraw remaining medication from the IV catheter before phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Withdraw any remaining medication from the IV catheter

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, inject phentolamine to clear the IV catheter and then remove the catheter.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Inject phentolamine to clear the IV catheter, then remove the catheter

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, administer phentolamine subcutaneously around the site in small divided doses of 0.2 mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In small divided doses (0.2 ml) administer dose subcutaneously around the site.

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, inject phentolamine into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Solution should be injected into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

atoms.canonical_statement: For infants, children, and adolescents, visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth are listed as signs of effective phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth at the site of extravasation are signs of effective treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, dilute phentolamine 5 mg in 10 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to yield 0.5 mg/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dilute 5 mg in 10 ml 0.9% Sodium Chloride injection (Yielding a concentration of 0.5 mg/ml)

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, withdraw remaining medication from the IV catheter before phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Withdraw any remaining medication from the IV catheter

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, inject a small amount of phentolamine to clear the IV catheter and then remove the catheter.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Inject a small amount of phentolamine to clear the IV catheter, then remove the catheter.

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, administer phentolamine subcutaneously around the site in small divided doses of 0.2 mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In small divided doses (0.2 ml) administer dose subcutaneously around the site.

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, inject phentolamine into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Solution should be injected into the affected area within 12 hours of extravasation.

atoms.canonical_statement: For adults, visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth are listed as signs of effective phentolamine treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Visible hyperemia and increased tissue warmth at the site of extravasation are signs of effective treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: Apply topical nitroglycerin 2% as a 1-inch strip to the site of ischemia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Topical Nitroglycerin 2%, 1-inch strip applied to the site of ischemia.

atoms.canonical_statement: Topical nitroglycerin 2% may be repeated every 8 hours if necessary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Can repeat every 8 hours if necessary.

atoms.canonical_statement: Use local comfort measures according to the treatment table or patient preference when not specified; ICN/SCN patients should not receive a compress.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Apply local comfort measures per table below or if not specified per patient preference ... ICN/SCN: Do not apply a compress

atoms.canonical_statement: For contrast extravasation, contact the provider and follow unit-specific guidelines; notify the original unit if the extravasation is discovered after discharge from that area.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Contact provider and follow unit guidelines for care of contrast extravasation ... Unit where extravasation occurred should be notified, if extravasation is found after discharge from that area.

atoms.canonical_statement: ICN/SCN should consult the WOC Team for any extravasation occurrence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ICN/SCN: Consult the WOC Team for any extravasation occurrence

atoms.canonical_statement: Pediatric services should consult the WOC Team for non-blanchable erythema and edema of an extremity after extravasation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Peds: Consult the WOC Team for all non blanchable erythema and edema noted to extremity after extravasation occurrence.

atoms.canonical_statement: Adult services should consult WOC Nursing for wounds caused by extravasation of medications that cause skin necrosis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adult: Consult the WOC Nursing Team for wounds resulting from the extravasation of medications that cause skin necrosis.

atoms.canonical_statement: Extravasation of known vesicants or corrosive medications is a reportable condition under the policy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Extravasation of known vesicants or corrosive medication.

atoms.canonical_statement: Increasing redness, induration, or ulceration is a reportable condition under the policy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Increasing size of redness, induration or ulceration.

atoms.canonical_statement: Increasing drainage from an ulcerated area is a reportable condition under the policy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Increasing amount of drainage from the ulcerated area.

atoms.canonical_statement: A temperature above 38.5 C orally in adults or above 37.1 C axillary in neonates and pediatric patients is a reportable condition under the policy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Temperature > 38.5 degrees C orally for adults and >37.1 degrees C axillary in neonates and pediatrics.

atoms.canonical_statement: For medications assigned a warm dry compress, apply a warm pack for 15 to 20 minutes four times daily during the first 24 to 48 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Apply warm pack for 15 - 20 minutes four times per day for the first 24 - 48 hours

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy states that warm compresses encourage local blood flow and modify medication viscosity to aid drug removal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Warm compresses will encourage local blood flow and modify viscosity of the medication to enhance drug removal

atoms.canonical_statement: For medications assigned a cold compress, apply it for at least 15 to 30 minutes four times daily during the first 48 to 72 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Apply cold compress for at least 15 - 30 minutes four times per day for the first 48 - 72 hours

atoms.canonical_statement: The policy recommends cold compresses to limit further inflammation, pain, and spread of extravasated medication.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cold compresses are recommended to prevent further inflammation/pain and limit the spread of extravasated medication.

atoms.canonical_statement: The DUHS treatment table lists warm compress and Hyaluronidase for Acyclovir extravasation, with no adjunctive or alternative therapy listed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Acyclovir Warm Hyaluronidase N/A
